PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

A dua is a supplication: words we say to ask Allah (S.W.T.) for help and protection. The Prophet (S.A.W) taught short duas for leaving the house and for entering it. In this sub-strand you will learn the words and meanings, recite them, and use them every day.

## Strand 5.0: Akhlaq (Moral Teachings)
Sub-strand 5.3.1: Dua (Supplication): Dua for Leaving and Entering the House
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) recite the dua for leaving and entering the house to seek Allah’s protection
b) use the dua in his/her day-to-day life
c) acknowledge the importance of using dua to get protection from Allah (S.W.T.)

## What this sub-strand covers
• Dua for Leaving and Entering the House

## Key inquiry questions
1. What do you recite when you leave home for school?
2. Why do you recite the dua when leaving and entering the house?

## Core competencies
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of speaking and teamwork as learners practise reciting the dua, in pairs/groups
• Creativity and imagination: the skill of making observations as learners role-play the dua on leaving and entering the house.

## Values
• Responsibility enhanced as learners role-play the dua on leaving and entering the house.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Self-esteem as learners recite the dua

## Links to other learning areas
• English as learners acquire new vocabularies in making supplication

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Teachings), Sub-strand 5.3.1 Dua (Supplication): Dua for Leaving and Entering the House
• The design's wording of the duas: leaving — "in the name of Allah I have placed my trust in Allah; there is no might and no power except by Allah"; entering — "In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our lord we depend"
• Sunan Abi Dawud and Jami at-Tirmidhi: the dua said on leaving the house

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: The dua for leaving the house

LESSON 1: THE DUA FOR LEAVING THE HOUSE
=======================================

## What you will learn
• Recite the dua for leaving the house.
• Give the meaning of the dua.
• Explain why a Muslim says this dua.

Curriculum outcomes: a) recite the dua for leaving and entering the house to seek Allah’s protection; c) acknowledge the importance of using dua to get protection from Allah (S.W.T.)

## Introduction
Every morning you step out of the door to go to school, the mosque or the market. Before that step, the Prophet (S.A.W) taught a short dua that places your journey in Allah's care.

## Notes
### What is dua?
Dua means supplication. It is calling on Allah (S.W.T.) to ask for good and for protection. A Muslim makes dua because all power belongs to Allah.

### The dua for leaving the house
The words, as given for this sub-strand, are:

Bismillahi tawakkaltu 'alallahi, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

The meaning is: "In the name of Allah, I have placed my trust in Allah; there is no might and no power except by Allah."

Learn it in small parts:

- Bismillahi — In the name of Allah
- tawakkaltu 'alallahi — I have placed my trust in Allah
- wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah — there is no might and no power except by Allah

### When to say it
Say this dua whenever you leave the house: in the morning for school, when you go to the mosque, when you are sent to the shop, and when the family travels.

### Why we say it
- We begin in Allah's name, so the journey is done for a good purpose.
- We admit that we depend on Allah, not on our own strength.
- "There is no might and no power except by Allah" means we cannot stay safe, succeed, or avoid harm unless Allah helps us.
- It is reported that a person who says this dua is answered with guidance, sufficiency and protection, and that the devils turn away from him.

Saying the dua does not replace looking both ways on the road or staying with people you trust. We use the means Allah has given us, and we still ask Him for protection. Acknowledging this dua shows that safety is from Allah (S.W.T.).

## Key words
• dua — a supplication; words said to ask Allah for help
• tawakkul — trusting Allah and relying on Him
• Bismillahi — In the name of Allah

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Amina is leaving for school. Put the three parts of the leaving dua in the correct order: (i) there is no might and no power except by Allah (ii) In the name of Allah (iii) I have placed my trust in Allah.

Working:
1. The dua begins with Bismillahi.
2. Next comes trust in Allah.
3. It ends with la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

Answer: (ii), (iii), (i)

## Activity: Recite the leaving dua
You will need: A chart or reference card with the dua and its meaning, Digital device if the teacher has a correct recitation
1. Listen to the teacher or a recording of the dua for leaving the house.
2. Repeat after the teacher, phrase by phrase, until you can say the full dua.
3. In pairs, one learner recites and the other gives the meaning, then swap.
4. Copy the dua and the meaning into your exercise book.

## Practice
1. Recite or write the dua for leaving the house.
2. What is the meaning of tawakkaltu 'alallahi?
3. What does 'there is no might and no power except by Allah' teach?
4. When should a Muslim say the dua for leaving the house?

## Summary
• The leaving dua begins with Bismillahi and trust in Allah.
• It reminds us that there is no power except by Allah.
• We say it to seek Allah's protection each time we go out.

### Answers to practice
1. Bismillahi tawakkaltu 'alallahi, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.
2. I have placed my trust in Allah.
3. We cannot stay safe or succeed unless Allah helps us.
4. Whenever he or she leaves the house, such as when going to school or the mosque.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: The dua for entering the house, and using both duas daily

LESSON 2: THE DUA FOR ENTERING THE HOUSE, AND USING BOTH DUAS DAILY
============================================================

## What you will learn
• Recite the dua for entering the house and give its meaning.
• Use the duas for leaving and entering in daily life.
• State why these duas matter.

Curriculum outcomes: a) recite the dua for leaving and entering the house to seek Allah’s protection; b) use the dua in his/her day-to-day life; c) acknowledge the importance of using dua to get protection from Allah (S.W.T.)

## Introduction
Coming home should be as mindful as going out. The Prophet (S.A.W) taught a dua to say as we enter, so that the house is entered in Allah's name and the family remembers who they depend on.

## Notes
### The dua for entering the house
The words taught for this sub-strand are:

Bismillahi walajna, wa bismillahi kharajna, wa 'ala Rabbina tawakkalna.

The meaning is: "In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we depend."

Learn it in three parts:

- Bismillahi walajna — In the name of Allah we enter
- wa bismillahi kharajna — in the name of Allah we leave
- wa 'ala Rabbina tawakkalna — and upon our Lord we depend

"Depend" here means we rely on Allah. The same word-family as tawakkul, trust, is in this dua.

### How to use the duas
- When you leave home, say the leaving dua.
- When you return, say the entering dua before or as you step in.
- If family members are inside, greet them with Assalamu alaikum.
- Say the duas calmly, not as a joke, and know the meaning so the heart is present.
- Practise every day until the words come easily. A dua you have memorised can be used for life.

### Why these duas are important
- They seek protection from Allah (S.W.T.) at the two moments when we cross the doorway.
- They remind the family that safety is not only from locks and walls, but from Allah.
- They train the tongue to remember Allah in ordinary acts. That remembrance is worship.
- A learner who uses them shows trust, discipline and thankfulness.

If you forget and remember after a few steps, say the dua then. The aim is to build a habit, not to feel hopeless after one miss. Parents and older siblings can remind one another gently.

## Key words
• walajna — we enter
• kharajna — we leave
• Rabb — Lord; Allah as the One who cares for and sustains us
• supplication — a humble request made to Allah

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Hassan leaves for madrasa and returns at noon. Which dua does he say at the door in the morning, and which does he say when he comes back?

Working:
1. Going out uses the dua of trust: Bismillahi tawakkaltu 'alallahi, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.
2. Coming in uses Bismillahi walajna, wa bismillahi kharajna, wa 'ala Rabbina tawakkalna.

Answer: Morning: the leaving dua. On return: the entering dua, then he greets the family.

## Activity: Role-play at the doorway
You will need: A chart of both duas, A space marked as a doorway
1. Practise reciting both duas in pairs until each learner can say them.
2. In groups, role-play a morning: one learner leaves for school and recites the leaving dua.
3. Role-play the return: the learner recites the entering dua and greets the family with salaam.
4. The class listens and gently corrects missed words. Each learner pledges to use the duas at home today.

## Practice
1. Write the dua for entering the house.
2. Give the meaning of the entering dua.
3. What should you say to family members who are at home when you enter?
4. Give one reason for using these duas every day.

## Summary
• The entering dua asks that we enter and leave in Allah's name and depend on our Lord.
• Use the leaving dua when you go out and the entering dua when you return.
• These duas seek protection from Allah and train us to remember Him.

### Answers to practice
1. Bismillahi walajna, wa bismillahi kharajna, wa 'ala Rabbina tawakkalna.
2. In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we depend.
3. Assalamu alaikum.
4. To seek Allah's protection, to remember that we depend on Him, or to make remembrance of Allah a daily habit.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 5.3.1 DUA (SUPPLICATION): DUA FOR LEAVING AND ENTERING THE HOUSE
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. What does the word dua mean?
   A. A type of food
   B. A supplication to Allah
   C. A school subject
   D. A kind of clothing

2. Which dua is said when leaving the house?
   A. Bismillahi walajna, wa bismillahi kharajna
   B. Bismillahi tawakkaltu 'alallahi, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
   C. Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullah
   D. Alhamdulillah

3. The meaning of tawakkaltu 'alallahi is…
   A. I have eaten
   B. I have placed my trust in Allah
   C. I am angry
   D. I am lost

4. How does the leaving dua complete the words 'there is no might and no power'?

5. Which is the correct meaning of the dua for entering the house?
   A. In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we depend
   B. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds
   C. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah
   D. Guide us to the straight path

6. What does walajna mean?
   A. we sleep
   B. we enter
   C. we eat
   D. we run

7. What should you do when you return home and people are inside?
   A. enter in silence and hide
   B. say the entering dua and greet them with salaam
   C. shout for food
   D. leave the door open

8. Why do Muslims recite a dua when leaving and entering the house?

9. If you forget the dua and remember it a few steps later, what should you do?
   A. Give up the habit
   B. Say it when you remember and try to build the habit
   C. Laugh about it
   D. Never leave the house again

10. What does la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah teach?
   A. people have all power
   B. there is no might and no power except by Allah
   C. doors protect us without Allah
   D. dua is only for adults
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 5.3.1 DUA (SUPPLICATION): DUA FOR LEAVING AND ENTERING THE HOUSE
========================================

1. B. A supplication to Allah
   Dua is calling on Allah to ask for help and protection.

2. B. Bismillahi tawakkaltu 'alallahi, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
   The leaving dua places trust in Allah and declares that power belongs to Him alone.

3. B. I have placed my trust in Allah
   Tawakkul is trust and reliance on Allah.

4. by Allah.
   The leaving dua ends with this declaration.

5. A. In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we depend
   This is the meaning given for the entering dua in this sub-strand.

6. B. we enter
   Bismillahi walajna means 'In the name of Allah we enter'.

7. B. say the entering dua and greet them with salaam
   The dua is said on entering, and salaam is the greeting for the family.

8. To seek Allah's protection and to show that they depend on Him.
   Safety and success come from Allah, so the doorway is a moment for remembrance.

9. B. Say it when you remember and try to build the habit
   The aim is a daily habit of remembrance, not despair after one miss.

10. B. there is no might and no power except by Allah
   The phrase means all strength and ability come from Allah.

3. Role-play the return: the learner recites the entering dua and greets the family with salaam.
4. The class listens and gently corrects missed words. Each learner pledges to use the duas at home today.

## Practice
1. Write the dua for entering the house.
2. Give the meaning of the entering dua.
3. What should you say to family members who are at home when you enter?
4. Give one reason for using these duas every day.

## Summary
• The entering dua asks that we enter and leave in Allah's name and depend on our Lord.
• Use the leaving dua when you go out and the entering dua when you return.
• These duas seek protection from Allah and train us to remember Him.

### Answers to practice
1. Bismillahi walajna, wa bismillahi kharajna, wa 'ala Rabbina tawakkalna.
2. In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we depend.
3. Assalamu alaikum.
4. To seek Allah's protection, to remember that we depend on Him, or to make remembrance of Allah a daily habit.

questions.question: What does the word dua mean?
questions.explanation: Dua is calling on Allah to ask for help and protection.

questions.question: Which dua is said when leaving the house?
options: Bismillahi tawakkaltu 'alallahi, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
questions.explanation: The leaving dua places trust in Allah and declares that power belongs to Him alone.

questions.question: The meaning of tawakkaltu 'alallahi is…
options: I have placed my trust in Allah
questions.explanation: Tawakkul is trust and reliance on Allah.

questions.question: How does the leaving dua complete the words 'there is no might and no power'?
questions.explanation: The leaving dua ends with this declaration.

questions.question: Which is the correct meaning of the dua for entering the house?
options: In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we depend
Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds
I bear witness that there is no god but Allah
Guide us to the straight path
questions.explanation: This is the meaning given for the entering dua in this sub-strand.

questions.question: What does walajna mean?
questions.explanation: Bismillahi walajna means 'In the name of Allah we enter'.

questions.question: What should you do when you return home and people are inside?
options: say the entering dua and greet them with salaam
questions.explanation: The dua is said on entering, and salaam is the greeting for the family.

questions.question: Why do Muslims recite a dua when leaving and entering the house?
questions.answer: To seek Allah's protection and to show that they depend on Him.
questions.explanation: Safety and success come from Allah, so the doorway is a moment for remembrance.

questions.question: If you forget the dua and remember it a few steps later, what should you do?
options: Say it when you remember and try to build the habit
questions.explanation: The aim is a daily habit of remembrance, not despair after one miss.

questions.question: What does la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah teach?
options: there is no might and no power except by Allah
questions.explanation: The phrase means all strength and ability come from Allah.
